title: Signatures of localization on the edge of a fractional topological insulator
authors: Yuzhuo Tian, Jinhong Park, Alexander D. Mirlin, Jukka I. Väyrynen
abstract: Recent experiments in van der Waals moiré materials have reported realizations of two-dimensional fractional topological insulators (FTIs). We study transport properties of FTI edges at filling factors $ν_{\text{FTI}} = 2(1\pm 1/n)$ with integer $n \geq 2$ (even or odd), each of which supports four counter-propagating edge modes. The edge modes can undergo partial localization, leaving two of the four edge modes conducting. We identify three distinct partial-localization channels and, for each channel, determine the reduced theory describing the remaining conducting modes, from which we obtain the minimal quasiparticle charge. We further explore transport properties of each partially localized phase and in particular determine the corresponding edge conductances. We demonstrate that measurements of the conductance together with the minimal quasiparticle charge provide a fingerprint that uniquely distinguishes the three partially localized phases.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how edge states in fractional topological insulators (FTIs) behave when they partially localize. By applying K-matrix formalism, the authors derive unique conductance signatures for three distinct localization channels. This provides a powerful experimental diagnostic tool, allowing researchers to identify the specific physical state of the FTI edge based on transport measurements.
main_problem: The study investigates the transport properties of edges in fractional topological insulators (FTIs) when partial localization occurs.
main_result: The combination of measured edge conductance and the minimal quasiparticle charge provides a unique fingerprint to distinguish between three distinct partially localized edge phases.
method: The authors use Wen's K matrix formalism to derive the reduced edge theory for different localization channels, calculating the resulting scattering matrices and conductances.
model_or_system: The system is an FTI realized in van der Waals moiré materials, characterized by filling factors $\nu_{\text{FTI}} = 2(1\pm 1/n)$. The edge theory involves analyzing the coupling between integer and fractional bosonic fields.
key_observables: Edge conductances ($G$), minimal quasiparticle charge ($Q_m$), and the four-terminal conductance matrix ($G$).
important_parameters: Filling factor $\nu_{\text{FTI}}$, integer $n \geq 2$, and the specific localization channels (e.g., backscattering, two-electron tunneling, superconductivity).
main_assumptions: Time-Reversal Symmetry (TRS) is preserved, and the analysis relies on the assumption of separate contactability for integer and fractional mode pairs.
figures_summary: The notes detail the derivation of scattering matrices ($S$) and conductance ($G$) for the three channels, showing distinct results for the four-terminal conductance matrices.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general edge theory using K-matrices, to analyzing the conditions for partial localization, and finally calculating the specific conductances and fingerprints for the three identified channels.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of edge transport in fractional topological systems provides concrete, measurable signatures (conductance vs. charge) that can be compared against experimental measurements in moiré materials, linking abstract topological theory to observable transport physics.
